title: Orbiting device with an interface dive
summary: A rendered phone turns through close and wide views while the camera travels across one interface, then dives into a detail and resolves to a quiet wordmark.
use_when: a mobile product needs a polished hero-object demo
one interface screen can support several camera framings
a silent product teaser needs continuous visual motion

look.type_style: compact sans serif UI, sentence case, regular to semibold, 2-4 % of frame height; small bold wordmark at about 3 % of frame height

sfx.event: device or camera begins an orbit sweep
hard reframe to a new device angle
camera accelerates into the interface detail

structure.shot: extreme close view of a rendered phone turning from its metal edge toward the interface
structure.camera: orbit from edge-biased to front-biased with push-in 1.00 -> 1.44 over 60 fr
structure.motion: camera follows easings.inOutSine for 60 fr; shallow focus remains on the upper interface

structure.shot: front-biased close view eases back and exposes more of the phone while keeping the interface readable
structure.camera: orbit continues toward the opposite edge with pull-out 1.00 -> 0.84 over 71 fr
structure.motion: camera follows easings.inOutSine for 71 fr; scale direction changes at the row start (plus or minus 0.25 s)

structure.shot: a tilted close view travels from search controls down to a grid of content cards on the same screen
structure.camera: dolly about -128,-363 px/s at 1920 width while the device continues its orbit over 121 fr
structure.motion: continuous easings.inOutSine dolly for 121 fr with depth-field focus held on the travelling screen region

structure.shot: the complete phone floats on white at a low diagonal angle with one long interface visible
structure.camera: orbit about 8 degrees with push-in 1.00 -> 1.09 over 120 fr
structure.motion: device and camera use easings.inOutSine for 120 fr; no independent interface animation is visible

structure.shot: the phone drops from the top edge as the camera dives into the lower content cards and navigation
structure.camera: push-in 1.00 -> 2.45 with a vertical dolly across the phone over 120 fr
structure.motion: camera acceleration uses easings.inExpo for about 75 fr, then easings.outQuint for about 45 fr (plus or minus 0.25 s)

structure.shot: a small centred wordmark resolves from pale partial letters on white, then holds
structure.camera: locked framing; no scale or position change over 90 fr
structure.motion: letters blur-in left to right with easings.outExpo over about 11 fr (plus or minus 0.25 s), then hold 79 fr

params.content: productName plus eyebrow, headline, metric, four cards and navigation labels for the local interface rebuild
params.deviceBody: neutral light or dark chassis colour with metallic edge highlights
params.cameraShots: five measured camera paths covering the device rows; each pose uses frames at the composition fps
params.background: flat light brand background, white by default
params.focus: 0-1 shadow and apparent depth strength for close device views
params.fps: composition fps, default 30; all structure frames scale from 30 fps

notes: Four hard cuts at 4.37, 8.40, 12.40 and 16.40 s; no audio or beat grid, so cut_on_beat is false (0/4). Exact camera yaw, focus distance, focal length, sub-0.25 s easing changes and entrance overshoot are not measurable from the 4 fps sheets. SFX planned by the glue rule, not measured. Phase B builds a deterministic local 2.5D DeviceOrbitStage because no true 3D phone stage is exported by the studio.
